title: 第二十三章 根须
content_zh:
内关穴的“松动”，如同在坚硬冻土上撬开的第一道裂缝，细微，却预示着其下深处，或许有截然不同的、可以生长的东西。

    接下来的三日，陈默过得极为“充实”。充实，意味着无时无刻不在与两种力量作斗争：一种是体内那被“撕开”的、残留的冰与火。寒髓液霸道凛冽的余威，与盘踞经脉深处的火毒残渣，虽已被打散、中和、化去大半，但残存的、细碎的冰碴与火星，依旧在他每次呼吸、每次气血运行时，带来针扎火燎般的刺痛，以及一种无处不在的、冰寒与灼热交替的、令人烦躁的“背景噪声”。他必须时刻运转苏芸所授的行气法与呼吸法，以那缕日渐温顺的水木灵气，如同最耐心的清道夫，一点点地、小心翼翼地将这些残渣“扫”出经脉，散入血肉，最终随着汗液、呼吸，被身体缓慢排出、代谢。

    另一种斗争，则来自于苏芸。

    似乎因陈默那番“以木疏水”的感悟，触及了某种她未曾预料、却又颇为认可的东西，接下来的草药教学中，苏芸的要求骤然提高，也更深、更系统了。

    她不再仅仅满足于教陈默辨认草药形态、药性、炮制，而是开始系统地阐述其背后的“理”。

    “天地万物，皆秉一气而生，然气有清浊，分阴阳，化五行。木主生发，其气条达，喜舒展，恶抑郁。对应人身，则肝胆属木，主疏泄，调情志，与筋膜、双目、乃至某些情绪的勃发相关。故木属性草药，多具疏通气机、解郁散结、舒筋活络、清肝明目之效。如你之前用过的透骨草，便是借其木性之‘达’，疏通筋骨淤滞；而定魂草，则是以其木性之‘稳’，安定浮动之神魂。”

    “水主润下，其性寒凉，趋静，藏。对应人身，则肾与膀胱属水，主藏精，司二便，与骨骼、耳窍、生殖及人体根本元气相关。水性草药，多具滋润、清热、利水、潜阳、填补精髓之功。如凝露果，便是取其水性之‘润’，滋养干涸经脉；寒髓液中的银线鲵髓液，则是以其极致水性之‘寒’，克制火毒之‘烈’。”

    她甚至用炭笔，在平整的石面上，画出简易的五行生克、脏腑对应图，将之前零散教过的草药，一一归类，纳入这个粗浅的框架之中。木生火，火生土，土生金，金生水，水生木。木克土，土克水，水克火，火克金，金克木。相生者，相助、滋生；相克者，制约、平衡。

    “你体内火毒，乃王炎火云掌力所化，性烈而燥，属‘火’之邪气。以寒髓液这等极致‘水’性之物克制，是以水克火之理。然水能克火，亦能耗水，过用则反伤己身根本。故需佐以木性行气法疏导，木可生火（但你所疏乃火毒，此‘生’为化散、引导其暴烈），亦可疏水（防寒毒淤积），此乃五行生克、以‘和’为贵之道在你体内的具体运用。”

    这些道理，对出身修仙宗门、哪怕只是最底层杂役的陈默而言，并非完全陌生。《引气诀》开篇亦有“一气分阴阳，阴阳化五行”的粗略提及。但从未有人像苏芸这般，将抽象空洞的“道理”，与具体实在的草药、伤势、乃至他自身的每一次气息运行、每一丝痛苦与缓解，如此紧密、清晰、层层剥茧般地联系起来。

    他听得极为专注，几乎要将每一个字都刻进脑海里。许多以往模糊的、知其然不知其所以然的困惑，在苏芸的讲解下，渐渐变得清晰。为何铁骨草性烈需配伍柔筋花？柔筋花性温，属土？土能制水（此处水指铁骨草的燥烈之“水”性？），亦能生金（金主收敛）以固其强筋之效？为何清心草与宁神花皆可安神，但清心草偏“清”心火（水克火），宁神花偏“滋养”心神（可能涉及木、土）？

    他开始尝试用这套刚刚接触、还极为粗浅的框架，去重新审视、理解周安笔记上的内容，去反思自己之前服用铁骨草汁液的莽撞，甚至去猜测苏芸为他调配的每一副汤药、每一种药膏背后，那精微的配伍思路。虽然大多数时候仍是一知半解，甚至猜测错误，但这种主动的、带着“理”去思考的过程本身，就让他对草药、对自身、乃至对“修炼”这件事的认知，发生了微妙而深刻的改变。

    苏芸似乎也乐见他这种“笨拙”却真诚的思考。在他提出一些基于新理解、但明显稚嫩甚至可笑的猜测时，她不再只是简短回答，偶尔会多解释几句，指出他思路中的亮点与谬误。她的态度依旧清冷，但陈默能感觉到，那层无形的、隔绝着她与这个世界的屏障，似乎因这种“教学相长”，而变得略微……通透了一丝。

    小荷依旧在旁听。她对那些五行生克、脏腑对应的“大道理”完全听不懂，大眼睛里满是茫然，但苏芸讲解具体草药形态、采摘、炮制、简单用途时，她却听得格外认真，甚至能提出一些关于如何更好地清洗某种带泥根茎、如何判断菌菇是否新鲜的实际问题。苏芸也会简短回应。这个沉默寡言的女孩，似乎将辨识草药、处理食材、打理石室，当成了自己在这陌生而危险境地里，唯一能抓住的、实实在在的“依靠”和“价值”。

    陈默的身体，在持续的调理和与冰火残渣的斗争中，缓慢而坚定地恢复着。左胸的疤痕开始软化，颜色变浅，虽依旧狰狞，但已不再牵绊胸廓的活动。内关穴的“通畅”感日益明显，气息流过时，虽然还有隐痛，但已能感受到一种细微的、力量传递的顺畅。更重要的是，随着那处关键节点的松动，以及行气法的持续练习，他隐约感觉到，丹田中那缕微弱的水木灵气，似乎比之前“听话”了些，对四肢末端劳宫、涌泉穴的感应，也比之前清晰了分毫。虽然距离真正自如地引动、操控外界灵气还差得远，但这无疑是巨大的鼓舞。

    第三日傍晚，苏芸检查完陈默的状况，尤其是仔细探查了他内关穴附近经脉的恢复情况，点了点头。

    “恢复尚可，残留的寒热之气也已化去大半。今夜子时，可尝试第二次。”她拿出那管寒髓液，但这次，她没有立刻交给陈默，而是又拿出另一个更小的、似乎是用某种兽骨磨制的浅口小碟，和一根纤细的骨针。

    “此次目标，膻中穴。此处乃宗气汇聚之所，亦是你之前修炼《引气诀》时，那‘墙’之所在。火毒盘踞颇深，与淤塞的‘墙’纠缠，凶险更甚内关。需更精细控制。”苏芸用骨针，从那竹筒中，极其小心地，只挑起比上次更小、约莫半滴的寒髓液，滴入骨碟中。那淡蓝色的液滴在骨碟中微微滚动，寒意凛然。“剂量减半，以策万全。且……”

    她顿了顿，看向陈默，眼中闪过一丝罕见的、类似征询的意味：“我需以金针，暂时封闭你膻中穴周围数处次要经脉，将寒髓液药力，尽可能约束、导向火毒核心，减少对周围完好经脉的冲击与误伤。但封脉之举，本身亦会带来滞涩与痛楚，且若你行气引导稍有偏差，被封经脉气血不畅，反易造成损伤。你……可信我？”

    信她？陈默看着苏芸平静无波的眼眸，那里倒映着篝火的微光，也倒映着他自己苍白却平静的脸。这一路走来，若无苏芸，他早已是黑风涧旁一具腐烂的尸体，或是杂役院医舍里一个苟延残喘的废人。她赠药、传法、护持、讲解，虽看似冷静甚至功利，但每一次援手，都精准地落在他最需要、也最无力的时刻。

    “我信。”他没有丝毫犹豫。

    苏芸眼中那丝征询之色散去，恢复了一贯的平静，点了点头。她没有多言，只是示意陈默坐好，褪去上身衣衫，露出瘦削却已不似最初那般枯槁的胸膛，以及左胸那道狰狞的疤痕。

    子时将至，石室内光线暗到极致，只有炭火的微光。小荷早已在角落沉沉睡去。

    苏芸先用清水净手，又以微火灼烤过那几枚银针。她站在陈默面前，微微俯身，神色专注至极，仿佛在进行一场神圣而精密的仪式。她先以手指在陈默膻中穴周围轻轻按压、感知，确认火毒盘踞最盛、与“墙”结合最紧密的几个点。然后，她捻起银针。

    第一针，刺入“中庭”穴，位于膻中下一寸。陈默只觉胸口微微一麻，随即，一股明显的滞涩感自该处传来，仿佛那一片的气血流动骤然减缓。

    第二针，“玉堂”，膻中上一寸六分。滞涩感加强。

    第三针，“紫宫”，玉堂上一寸六分。

    第四针，“华盖”，紫宫上一寸六分……

    苏芸下针极稳、极准，每一针落下，陈默都能感觉到膻中穴周围一片区域的经脉，被逐渐“圈禁”、“孤立”开来，气血运行变得异常迟缓、沉重，胸口仿佛压上了一块无形的石头，呼吸都开始有些不畅。但同时，那种因火毒盘踞而带来的、持续的、隐隐的灼热烦躁感，也在这种“封禁”下，被暂时隔绝、凸显出来，变得更为清晰、集中，仿佛一团被压缩、囚禁在方寸之地的、躁动不安的火焰。

    八针落下，形成一个以膻中穴为中心、约莫巴掌大小的无形“牢笼”。苏芸额角已渗出细密的汗珠，脸色比平日更白，显然这番金针封脉，对她而言消耗亦是不小。她略作调息，然后拿起那根骨针，从骨碟中沾起那半滴寒髓液。

    “准备。”她低声道，声音带着一丝不易察觉的紧绷。

    陈默深吸一口气，闭上双眼，将心神沉入那片被“封禁”的、灼热而凝滞的区域。体内那缕水木灵气，已缓缓调动，蓄势待发。

    苏芸手腕轻抖，骨针带着那点淡蓝幽光，轻轻点在了陈默膻中穴正中央！

    “嗤——！”

    仿佛烧红的铁水，滴入万载寒冰之中！一股比上次在内关穴强烈十倍不止的、极寒与极热瞬间对撞、爆发的恐怖力量，在陈默膻中穴那方寸之间，轰然炸开！
content_en:
The "looseness" of the Neiguan point is like the first crack pried open in the hard frozen soil. It is subtle, but it indicates that there may be something completely different and capable of growing deep below.
In the next three days, Chen Mo lived an extremely "fulfilling" life.Fulfillment means fighting against two forces all the time: one is the remaining ice and fire that have been "torn apart" in the body.Although most of the overbearing and biting lingering power of the cold marrow liquid and the poisonous residue entrenched deep in his meridians have been dispersed, neutralized, and dissolved, the remaining fine ice particles and sparks still bring a stinging pain like needles and fire every time he breathes and every time his qi and blood circulate, as well as a ubiquitous and irritating "background noise" that alternates between cold and scorching heat.He must always use the qi movement and breathing methods taught by Su Yun, and use the increasingly docile water and wood spiritual energy, like the most patient scavenger, to "sweep" these residues out of the meridians bit by bit and disperse into the flesh and blood, and finally be slowly excreted and metabolized by the body with sweat and breathing.
Another kind of struggle comes from Su Yun.
It seemed that Chen Mo's insight about "using wood to repel water" touched something that she had not expected but recognized quite a bit. In the following herbal medicine teaching, Su Yun's requirements suddenly increased, becoming deeper and more systematic.
She was no longer just content to teach Chen Mo to identify the form, medicinal properties, and preparation of herbal medicines, but began to systematically explain the "principles" behind them.
"All things in the world are born with one Qi. However, Qi is clear and turbid, divided into yin and yang, and transforms into the five elements. Wood governs hair growth, and its Qi is well-organized. It likes to be relaxed and hates depression. Corresponding to the human body, the liver and gallbladder belong to wood, which governs relaxation and flirting. It is related to fascia, eyes, and even the eruption of certain emotions. Therefore.Herbs with wood properties have the effect of clearing qi, relieving stagnation and dispersing stagnation, relaxing muscles and collaterals, clearing the liver and improving eyesight.For example, the wood-like herb that you used before is used to clear the stagnant muscles and bones due to its woody nature;while the soul-stabilizing herb is used to stabilize the floating spirit due to its woody nature."
"Water is responsible for moisturizing the lower body, and its nature is cold and cool, tending to calm and store away. Corresponding to the human body, the kidneys and bladder belong to water, which store essence and serve as excrement. It is related to bones, ears, reproduction and the basic vitality of the human body. Water-based herbs are mostly nourishing, clearing away heat,It has the function of diluting water, replenishing yang, and replenishing the essence.For example, the "moistening" nature of the condensation fruit is used to nourish the dry meridians; the silver-threaded salamander marrow liquid in the cold marrow liquid uses the "cold" nature of the water to restrain the "violence" of fire poison."
She even used charcoal to draw a simple map of the five elements and the internal organs on a flat stone surface, and classified the herbs she had been taught scatteredly before into this rough framework.Wood generates fire, fire generates earth, earth generates metal, metal generates water, and water generates wood.Wood defeats earth, earth defeats water, water defeats fire, fire defeats metal, and metal defeats wood.Those that are in harmony with each other help and breed; those that are in conflict with each other are in restraint and balance.
"The fire poison in your body is transformed by the power of Wang Yanhuo Yun's palm. It is strong and dry in nature and belongs to the evil spirit of 'fire'. Using cold marrow liquid and other extremely 'water' properties to restrain it is the principle of using water to overcome fire. However, water can restrain fire and also consume water. If used too much, it will damage the root of the body. Therefore.It needs to be channeled by the method of moving Qi of the nature of wood. Wood can generate fire (but what you are sparing is fire poison, and this "generation" is to dissipate and guide its violence), and it can also repel water (preventing the accumulation of cold poison). This is the specific application of the principle of "harmony" in your body."
These principles are not completely unfamiliar to Chen Mo, who was born in a sect that cultivates immortals, even if he is just a servant at the lowest level.There is also a rough mention in the opening chapter of "Qi-Yin Jue" that "One Qi divides Yin and Yang, and Yin and Yang transform into the five elements."But no one has ever connected the abstract and empty "principles" with concrete and real herbs, injuries, and even every movement of his own breath, every trace of pain and relief like Su Yun, so closely, clearly, and like peeling off layers of cocoons.
He listened with great concentration, almost carving every word into his mind.Many confusions that were vague in the past, and that we knew what was happening but didn't know why, gradually became clear under Su Yun's explanation.Why does Tiegucao have strong properties and needs to be combined with Roujinhua?Roujin flower is warm in nature and belongs to earth.Earth can control water (water here refers to the strong "water" nature of Tiegucao?), and it can also produce metal (metal is the main astringent) to consolidate its muscle-strengthening effect?Why can both Qingxincao and Ningshenhua soothe the mind, but Qingxincao "clears" the heart fire (water overcomes fire), while Ningshenhua "nourishes" the mind (may involve wood and earth)?
He began to try to use this new and very superficial framework to re-examine and understand the contents of Zhou An's notes, to reflect on his recklessness in taking the iron bone grass juice before, and even to guess the subtle compatibility ideas behind every decoction and ointment that Su Yun prepared for him.Although most of the time he still had only a partial understanding and even made wrong guesses, the process of proactively thinking with "reason" itself caused subtle and profound changes in his understanding of herbs, himself, and even "cultivation".
Su Yun seemed to be happy to see his "clumsy" but sincere thinking.When he proposed some speculations based on new understandings that were obviously naive or even ridiculous, she no longer just gave short answers, but occasionally explained a few more sentences and pointed out the highlights and fallacies in his thinking.Her attitude was still cold, but Chen Mo could feel that the invisible barrier that separated her from the world seemed to have become slightly... transparent due to this "teaching and mutual learning".
Xiao He was still listening.She didn't understand the "big principles" about the five elements and the corresponding internal organs at all, and her big eyes were full of confusion. But when Su Yun explained the specific forms, picking, processing, and simple uses of herbal medicines, she listened very carefully. She was even able to ask some practical questions about how to better clean certain muddy rhizomes and how to judge whether mushrooms were fresh.Su Yun will also respond briefly.This taciturn girl seems to regard identifying herbs, processing ingredients, and taking care of stone chambers as the only real "reliance" and "value" she can grasp in this strange and dangerous situation.
Chen Mo's body recovered slowly but surely through continuous conditioning and fighting against the ice and fire residue.The scar on the left chest began to soften and became lighter in color. Although it was still hideous, it no longer hindered the movement of the chest.The "smoothness" of the Neiguan point is becoming increasingly obvious. When the breath flows through, although there is still a dull pain, a subtle and smooth power transmission can be felt.More importantly, with the loosening of the key node and the continuous practice of the Qi Movement method, he vaguely felt that the weak water and wood spiritual energy in the Dantian seemed to be more "obedient" than before, and the induction of the Laogong and Yongquan points at the ends of the limbs was also clearer than before.Although it is still far from being able to truly freely induce and control external spiritual energy, this is undoubtedly a huge encouragement.
On the evening of the third day, Su Yun checked Chen Mo's condition, especially the recovery of the meridians near his Neiguan point, and nodded.
"The recovery is acceptable, and most of the remaining cold and hot energy has been eliminated. You can try it a second time tonight." She took out the tube of cold marrow liquid, but this time, she did not hand it to Chen Mo immediately. Instead, she took out another smaller, shallow-mouthed dish that seemed to be ground with some kind of animal bone, and a slender bone needle.
"The target this time is the Tanzhong point. This is where the sect energy gathers, and it is also where the 'wall' was when you practiced the 'Qi-Inducing Technique' before. The fire poison is entangled very deep, entangled with the blocked 'wall', and the danger is even more dangerous in the inner pass. More precise control is needed." Su Yun used a bone needle to pick up only half a drop of cold marrow liquid from the bamboo tube, which was smaller than last time, and dripped it into the bone dish.The light blue liquid droplets rolled slightly in the bone dish, giving it a chilling feeling."Half the dose, just to be safe. And..."
She paused and looked at Chen Mo, with a rare hint of inquiry flashing in her eyes: "I need to use golden needles to temporarily seal several minor meridians around your Tanzhong point, and use the power of the cold marrow liquid to restrain and direct it to the core of the fire poison as much as possible., to reduce the impact and accidental damage to the surrounding intact meridians, but the act of sealing the meridians will also cause stagnation and pain, and if your Qi guidance is slightly deviated, the blocked meridians will be blocked, which may cause damage."
Believe her?Chen Mo looked at Su Yun's calm eyes, which reflected the dim light of the bonfire and his own pale but calm face.Along the way, if it hadn't been for Su Yun, he would have been a rotting corpse beside the Black Wind Stream, or a cripple lingering in the hospital.She gave medicine, taught Dharma, supported and explained. Although she seemed calm and even utilitarian, every helping hand fell precisely at the moment when he needed it most and was at his weakest.
"I believe it." He didn't hesitate at all.
The questioning look in Su Yun's eyes dissipated, she returned to her usual calmness, and nodded.She didn't say much, but just motioned for Chen Mo to sit down and took off his upper body clothes, revealing his thin but not as withered chest as before, as well as the hideous scar on his left chest.
At midnight, the light in the stone room was extremely dark, with only the faint light of the charcoal fire.Xiaohe had already fallen asleep in the corner.
Su Yun first washed her hands with water, and then burned the silver needles with low fire.She stood in front of Chen Mo, leaning slightly, her expression extremely focused, as if she was performing a sacred and precise ritual.She first used her fingers to gently press and feel around Chen Mo's Tanzhong point to confirm the points where the fire poison was most entrenched and most closely connected with the "wall".Then, she twisted the silver needle.
The first needle is inserted into the "Zhongting" point, located one inch below the center of the tan.Chen Mo only felt a slight numbness in his chest, and then an obvious sense of stagnation came from there, as if the flow of qi and blood in that area suddenly slowed down.
The second needle, "Yutang", is one inch and six points above the middle of the tan.The feeling of sluggishness is enhanced.
The third needle, "Purple Palace", is one inch and six points on the Yutang.
The fourth needle, "Huagai", one inch and six points on the purple palace...
Su Yun placed the needle very steadily and accurately. With each needle drop, Chen Mo could feel that the meridians in the area around the Tanzhong point were gradually "confined" and "isolated". The flow of Qi and blood became extremely slow and heavy.
